title: bug: the agent launchers read .moe/daemon.json with no size cap
description:
Objective: bound the launchers' reads of .moe/daemon.json. Both twins read the whole file:
- scripts/moe-agent.sh pre-flight parses it with python json.load(open(...)) several times: the daemon check (~:1469-1490) and the start wait loop (~:1581);
- scripts/moe-agent.ps1 uses Get-Content -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json (~:570).
This is a sibling of task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (the JetBrains reader, 64 KiB cap). daemon.json is repository content.

Deliverable:
- In both twins, every daemon.json read goes through one bounded read of at most 65537 bytes. In Python that is open(p, 'rb').read(65537); in PowerShell, a FileStream read into a 65537-byte buffer.
- A larger file is handled exactly like an unparseable one: the sh's existing '[WARN] Failed to parse daemon.json' path, or the ps1's existing catch. The launcher then starts its own daemon as today.
- String parity between the twins is kept.

Not in scope:
- moe-team.{sh,ps1} and moe-call.sh: they never read the file's contents (moe-call delegates to moe-proxy, a sibling task);
- the WSL foreign-daemon probing logic.

Depends on the live wrapper tasks task-bdf6db6f65b04a009c88c1e49aed3848, task-bc8410afe7144ddda804b60af000864d and task-c2a900aa5107479aa4c630f1b3837ed0, and through bdf6db6f on task-6aa460bb. All of them edit both launchers, so these edits must wait.

Verification: bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && node --test scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh. The new test runs the real sh block, and the real ps1 block wherever Windows PowerShell 5.1 or pwsh 7 exists.
definitionOfDone: Every daemon.json read in moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 goes through a bounded read of at most 65537 bytes, and a larger file takes the existing unparseable path.

New scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs runs the real launcher blocks against a 65536-byte and a 65537-byte daemon.json, on bash and on every PowerShell engine available. A missing engine is reported and never counted as a pass.
bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes, and moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM.
Fresh bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && node --test scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN for sh, in the MIRROR ($M/scripts/moe-agent.sh). Step 4 replays it into scripts/moe-agent.sh.

1. Add, right after wsl_gateway_host() and before '# Start daemon if needed':

# daemon.json is repository content: read at most 64 KiB + 1 byte and treat a
# larger file like unparseable JSON (python exits non-zero). Same cap as the
# daemon, proxy, IDE plugins and moe-agent.ps1's Read-MoeDaemonJsonText.
daemon_json_field() { # $1 = daemon.json path, $2 = key; prints the value
    $PYTHON_CMD -c 'import json,sys
d=open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read(65537)
if len(d)>65536: sys.exit("daemon.json is larger than 64 KiB")
sys.stdout.write(str(json.loads(d).get(sys.argv[2],"")))' "$1" "$2"
}

Notes on the helper:
- $PYTHON_CMD stays unquoted, like every existing call: it is 'py -3' on some Windows boxes.
- json.loads accepts bytes, including a UTF-8 BOM.
- sys.stdout.write adds no newline, so Windows Python cannot leave a '\r' inside $(...).

2. Replace the four inline reads with the helper, keeping each site's redirections.
- PID check:
  PID_EXIT_CODE=0
  PID_OUTPUT=$(daemon_json_field "$DAEMON_INFO" pid 2>&1) || PID_EXIT_CODE=$?
  This replaces the old 'PID_EXIT_CODE=$?' line. The '||' is REQUIRED. Under the script's set -e, the old unguarded assignment exits the launcher silently on ANY parse failure, so its own '[WARN] Failed to parse daemon.json' branch was unreachable (verified). Now an oversize or malformed file prints that WARN, leaves PID empty and starts a daemon. That matches moe-agent.ps1, which already does so from its catch.
- DAEMON_PORT=$(daemon_json_field "$DAEMON_INFO" port 2>/dev/null || echo "")
- DAEMON_PROJECT=$(daemon_json_field "$DAEMON_INFO" projectPath 2>/dev/null || echo "")
- In the start wait loop: NEW_PID=$(daemon_json_field "$DAEMON_INFO" pid 2>/dev/null || echo "")

Error handling is otherwise unchanged:
- the foreign-daemon probe;
- the stale-PID delete, which only follows a successful parse with a dead PID and never happens for size;
- the start and wait logic.

Then run bash -n "$M/scripts/moe-agent.sh" and the WSL mirror run: bash cases (a), (b) and (c) are green.

- Both Get-Content reads are now `Read-MoeDaemonJsonText $daemonInfoPath | ConvertFrom-Json`, each inside its existing try/catch.

One deviation from the plan text: the helper opens `[IO.File]::OpenRead((Convert-Path -LiteralPath $Path))`, not `OpenRead($Path)`.
- I verified on powershell.exe that Resolve-Path on a UNC project (\\localhost\c$\Windows) returns `Microsoft.PowerShell.Core\FileSystem::\\...`. Join-Path keeps that form, Test-Path accepts it, and [IO.File]::OpenRead throws "The given path's format is not supported.".
- So the plan's helper would make a UNC project with a live daemon read as not running and try to start a second daemon. Today's Get-Content reads that path fine.
- Convert-Path yields the plain provider path. Test-Path has already confirmed the file exists, and any Convert-Path error lands in the same catch.
- New ps1 case: 'a provider-qualified daemon.json path (a UNC project) is read'. The static check now also requires `Convert-Path -LiteralPath`.

  - with `-gt 65537`, the 65537-byte case fails.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the mirror into the checkout, then run the verification gate ONCE.

1. Compare-and-swap. cmp the checkout's scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 against $M/pristine/. If either changed since the mirror was taken (another task landed), redo steps 2-3 on fresh copies and re-run both legs first.

2. Replay with your edit tool (Claude: Edit). That also gives the wrapper's TOOL attribution witness on a contested launcher path; never use a shell cp over a live launcher.
   - Order the hunks so every intermediate file stays valid for live seats: each helper first, then its call sites, and the sh PID hunk with its guard in one edit.
   - Create scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs from the mirror copy.

3. cmp all three checkout files against the mirror: they must be byte-identical. head -c3 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | od -An -tx1 must show ef bb bf.

4. Gate, on WSL, in place (it reads the scripts and writes only temp dirs):
   bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && node --test scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh
   Exit 0 is required. On WSL the PowerShell cases are reported as skipped.

5. Windows leg, labelled Windows evidence: cmd.exe /d /c "node --test scripts\tests\daemon-json-cap.test.mjs" from the repo root. It must show zero failed and zero skipped.

complete_task gets { command: 'bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && node --test scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh', exitCode, outputTail }, plus the Windows leg's tail.

Error handling: if the in-place gate fails, restore the launchers from $M/pristine/ at once. First cmp that nobody else changed them. Then fix the problem in the mirror, re-test and replay. Never leave a failing launcher in the checkout, and never weaken an assertion.

- Replayed with the Edit tool, so the wrapper sees TOOL-tier witnesses. Order: each helper first, then its call sites, and the sh PID read plus its `||` guard in one edit. The test file was created with Write.
- cmp: all 3 checkout files are byte-identical to the mirror. moe-agent.ps1 starts with ef bb bf and has 0 CR.
- Diff: moe-agent.sh +15/-5 and moe-agent.ps1 +21/-2. The new test file is 183 lines.

Gate on WSL, in place, `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && node --test scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`: GATE_EXIT=0.
- node --test: 14 tests, 4 pass, 0 fail, 10 skipped (PS 5.1 is Windows-only; no pwsh on linux).
- PASS parity-check.sh.

Windows evidence, `cmd.exe /d /c "node --test scripts\tests\daemon-json-cap.test.mjs"` from the repo root: WIN_EXIT=0, node v24.16.0, 14 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. Engines were Git Bash, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7, including ParseFile.

No other launcher test slices the edited blocks (checked with grep). postflight passes --no-start-daemon.

Adversarial review of the 3-file diff (`git diff -- <own paths>`). It changed no bytes, so step 4 stands.

Checks against the plan's list:
- Boundary: sh reads read(65537) and rejects >65536. ps1 uses byte[] 65537 and rejects -gt 65536. The 65536/65537 pair runs on every engine. Mutants -gt 65537 and no-Convert-Path were each caught on both PS engines.
- ps1 handle: OpenRead sits before the try, and the throw lands in finally → Dispose. If Convert-Path or OpenRead fails, no stream exists, and the caller's catch handles it.
- 'py -3': $PYTHON_CMD is unquoted. Verified with PYTHON_CMD='env python3'.
- set -e guard: only the PID read needed `PID_EXIT_CODE=0 … || PID_EXIT_CODE=$?`. port, projectPath and NEW_PID keep `2>/dev/null || echo ""`.
- No delete: an oversize file is never deleted, because only the stale-PID branch deletes, after a successful parse. The test asserts the file is still 65537 bytes afterwards.
- WARN text: the oversize WARN is python's one-line sys.exit message. A malformed file prints python's traceback ending in the JSONDecodeError line/col. That is the pre-existing message shape, and it never includes file content.
- Test hygiene: rmSync runs in finally, and every spawnSync and probe has a 60 s timeout. All anchors include their leading newline.
- No daemon.json read remains: moe-call.sh:194 only runs `[ -f ]`, moe-team never reads the file, and local-runner has its own 16 KiB cap. No name collisions.

Concurrency: the daemon writes daemon.json via tmp + renameSync, so nothing holds daemon.json open for write. OpenRead's FileShare.Read therefore behaves like Get-Content's FileShare.ReadWrite and python's open(). The brief rename-blocking window while we hold a read handle is pre-existing.

TOCTOU: a file deleted between `[ -f ]` and python now WARNs and starts a daemon. Before, the launcher aborted silently.

Intended behavior change: on sh, a malformed or vanished daemon.json now WARNs and starts a daemon, matching ps1, instead of silently aborting the launcher under set -e.

Residuals, pre-existing, noted only:
- A daemon is started while one is live but its daemon.json is unreadable (same as the ps1 catch).
- A FIFO at .moe/daemon.json blocks the open; git cannot commit a FIFO.
- On ps1, a UTF-16 daemon.json (only by hand edit; the daemon writes UTF-8) no longer decodes. The daemon, proxy and plugin readers decode UTF-8 too.

Filed task-b8b8faba (LOW, dependsOn this task): CI's explicit node --test lists include neither daemon-json-cap.test.mjs nor seat-registration.test.mjs.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Editing the launchers in place: rejected. Live seats hot-reload moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 on every change and re-run this pre-flight, so a buggy intermediate state could make every reloading seat abort or start a duplicate daemon. A mirror under the Windows temp lets both WSL and Windows node test the exact bytes before they land. (2) Leaving the PID read unguarded: rejected. Under set -e the WARN branch the task names is unreachable (verified: exit 1). The guard is what makes 'handled like unparseable' and 'starts its own daemon as today' true. (3) Adding the oversize message to parity-check.sh: rejected. It would need the .ps1 twin as well, two more files; the new test asserts the shared string. (4) A large-file or /dev/zero test: rejected. The cap is by construction (read(65537), byte[65537]), the boundary pair proves the threshold, and huge fixtures risk runaway memory.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- moe-agent.sh runs under `set -e` (line 5). The daemon check (~:1465-1538) does four python json.load(open()) reads: the PID one is unguarded with 2>&1; port and projectPath use 2>/dev/null || echo ""; the wait loop ~:1581 does the same.
- PYTHON_CMD can be 'py -3', so it is expanded unquoted.
- moe-agent.ps1 sets $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' (:103). Its reads are at :569 and :609, each inside a try/catch.
- Read-MoeGateTail (:1666) is the house bounded-read idiom.
- The ps1 file is UTF-8 with BOM and LF endings.
- postflight.sh always passes --no-start-daemon, so the new test is the only coverage of this block.
- seat-registration.test.mjs has the ENGINES matrix and probe to copy.
- This WSL box reaches Windows node 24.16, Git Bash, Python 3.14, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7 through cmd.exe.
planningNotes.risks:
- Hot reload: never leave untested launcher bytes in the checkout (mirror, then compare-and-swap, then an Edit replay).
- A bare-substring anchor slices the FOREIGN branch, so anchors must include the newline.
- The ps1 BOM must survive.
- Behavior change: a malformed daemon.json now starts a daemon on sh instead of aborting the launcher (parity with ps1).
- Prerequisites edit the same launchers; locate everything by anchor after they land.
